q: A teacher wants every student to receive an individual editable copy of the same planning template in Classroom. Which attachment option is best?
choices: Make a copy for each student
exp: Make a copy for each student gives each learner an individual copy while preserving the original.

q: You are preparing an assignment now but do not want students to see it until Monday morning. What should you do?
choices: Post it now and delete it later
exp: Scheduling controls when the assignment becomes visible.

q: Which Google tool is the best fit for collecting structured responses from a class survey?
exp: Forms is built for structured surveys, quizzes, and response collection.

q: You need a class information site with pages, links, images, and embedded resources without writing code. Which tool is most appropriate?
exp: Sites is designed for simple collaborative websites.

q: Which tool is best for creating a recurring weekly planning meeting and inviting colleagues?
exp: Calendar manages recurring events, guests, reminders, and conferencing.

q: A teacher wants students to submit a short reflection with one paragraph and a rating from 1–5. Which solution is most efficient?
choices: Create a Form with paragraph and linear-scale questions
Create a new Meet for every student
Ask students to rename a Drive folder
Create a Site page for every response
exp: Forms provides suitable question types and central response collection.

q: You want to create a short quiz that can automatically grade multiple-choice items. Which tool is the best starting point?
exp: Forms can be configured as a quiz with answer keys and points.

q: A teacher wants students to build a slide deck collaboratively. Which tool should be used?
You need to draft a lesson plan with headings, links, comments, and collaborative editing. Which tool is the best fit?
exp: Docs is designed for collaborative text documents.

q: A class needs one central folder containing instructions, reference files, and student resources. What is the best first step?
choices: Create a clearly named Drive folder
Publish every file to the web
exp: A dedicated Drive folder creates a manageable resource structure.

q: Which two actions are useful when setting up a new Classroom assignment? (Select two.)
choices: Make the class public on the web
exp: Clear instructions and an appropriate due date are core assignment setup actions.

q: A teacher wants students to choose a time slot for a short conference. Which Google Workspace approach best fits the need?
choices: Use Calendar scheduling/appointment features where available
Use a Sheet filter view only
exp: Calendar is the most suitable tool for managing time slots and meetings.

q: Which feature helps make a long Google Doc easier to navigate?
exp: Heading styles create structure and improve navigation.

q: Students will work in small groups on presentations. What is the most efficient file setup?
choices: Create one shared Slides file per group with edit access for group members
Create a public Site for every student
Send each group screenshots of a slide
exp: A shared presentation gives group members a common editable workspace.

q: A teacher wants to post a resource in Classroom without requiring students to submit work. Which type of post is most appropriate?
exp: A Material post is appropriate for resources that do not require submission.

q: You want a form to require students to answer an important question before submitting. Which setting should you use?
exp: Required questions must be completed before submission.
